(a) a {@item scholar's pack|phb} or (b) {@item explorer's pack|phb}

subclass.name: Order of the Wu Jen
subclassFeatures: Order of the Wu Jen|Psion|THICC-PSION|Wu Jen|THICC-PSION|1

classFeature.name: Psionics
entries: As a student of psionics, you can master and use psionic talents and disciplines. Psionics is a special form of magic use, distinct from spellcasting as it does not use The Weave.

entries.name: Psionic Talents
entries: A psionic talent is a minor psionic effect you have mastered. At 1st level, you know two psionic talents of your choice. You learn additional talents of your choice at higher levels. The Talents Known column of the Psion table shows the total number of talents you know at each level; when that number goes up for you, choose a new talent.

entries.name: Psionic Disciplines
entries: A psionic discipline is a rigid set of mental exercises that allows a psion to manifest psionic power. A psion masters only a few disciplines at a time.

At 1st level, you know one psionic discipline of your choice. The Disciplines Known column of the Psion table shows the total number of disciplines you know at each level; when that number goes up for you, choose a new discipline. Disciplines learned this way may be chosen regardless of what Psionic Order they are associated with.

entries.name: Psi Points
entries: You have an internal reservoir of energy that can be devoted to psionic disciplines you know. This energy is represented by psi points. Each psionic discipline describes effects you can create with it by spending a certain number of psi points. A psionic talent requires no psi points.

The number of psi points you have is based on your psion level, as shown in the Psi Points column of the Psion table. The number shown for your level is your psi point maximum. Your psi point total returns to its maximum when you finish a long rest. The number of psi points you have can’t go below 0 or over your maximum.

entries.name: Psi Limit
entries: Though you have access to a potent amount of psionic energy, it takes training and practice to channel that energy. There is a limit on the number of psi points you can spend to activate a psionic discipline. The limit is based on your psion level, as shown in the Psi Limit column of the Psion table. For example, as a 3rd-level psion, you can spend no more than 3 psi points on a discipline each time you use it, no matter how many psi points you have.

entries.name: Psychic Focus
entries: Merely holding a reservoir of psi points in mind gives psions a special energy. Psionic characters can put that energy to work without actually expending psi points.

As an action, if you have 1 or more psi points available, you can focus your psionic energy in meditation on one of your psionic disciplines to draw ongoing benefits from it. If you attempt to do this in combat, any enemies that can reach you gain an attack of opportunity on you. For each attack that hits, you must pass a {@status concentration||concentration} saving throw, or the meditation is disrupted. Otherwise, choose one of your psionic disciplines and gain its psychic focus benefit, which is detailed in that discipline’s description. The benefit lasts until you are {@condition Incapacitated|phb} or until you attempt to meditate again to choose a different focus benefit. The benefit does not end if you expend all of your psi points.
You can have only one psychic focus benefit at a time, and using the psychic focus of one discipline doesn’t limit your ability to use other disciplines.

entries.name: Psionic Ability
entries: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your psionic disciplines. You use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a psionic discipline or when making an attack roll with one.

classFeature.name: Psionic Order feature
entries: At 1st level, you gain a feature from your Psionic Order.

classFeature.name: Psionic Recovery
entries: By 2nd level, you discover a way to clear your mind of everything, allowing you to regain some psi points. Once per day, you can spend a short rest completely in meditation as if you were concentrating on a discipline, ending any current active psychic focus, psionic talents, and psionic disciplines. At the end of the short rest, you regain psi points equal to your psion level.

classFeature.name: Telepathy
entries: At 2nd level, your mind awakens to the ability to communicate via telepathy. You can telepathically speak to any creature you can see within 120 feet of you in this manner. The creature understands you only if the two of you share a language. You can speak telepathically in this way to one creature at a time. In combat, you may do this as a free action once per turn.

classFeature.name: Psionic Order feature
entries: At 3rd level, you gain a feature from your Psionic Order.

classFeature.name: Feat
entries: When you reach 4th level, you gain a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Psionic Versatility
entries: Whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Feat feature, you can do one of the following:

items: Replace one psionic talent you know with a different one from the Psionic Talents list.

Replace one psionic discipline you know with a different one from the Psionic Disciplines list. You can only do this if you would still have at least one discipline belonging to your order after it is replaced.

classFeature.name: Dispel Psionics
entries: At 5th level, you gain the ability to disrupt psionic effects. As an action, you choose one creature, object, or psionic effect within 120 feet of yourself, expending a number of psi points between 5 and your psi limit. Any psionic effect created by an amount of psi points equal to the amount of psi points expended to use this feature or lower immediately ends. For each psionic effect created with more psi points than you expended, you must make an {@skill Arcana} ability check. The DC for each check is equal to 15 + the amount of psi points expended more than your own. On each success, the respective effect ends.

classFeature.name: Psionic Order feature
entries: At 6th level, you gain a feature from your Psionic Order.

classFeature.name: Universal Telepathy
entries: By 7th level, your mastery of telepathy allows you to talk to creatures using images and ideas. You don’t need to share a language with the creature for it to understand your telepathic messages, but the creature must be able to understand at least one language or be telepathic itself. Additionally, you can share sights you have seen, sounds you have heard, or any other visual or auditory sense you can think of with the target of your telepathy.

classFeature.name: Psionic Order feature
entries: At 8th level, you gain a feature from your Psionic Order.

classFeature.name: Feat
entries: When you reach 8th level, you gain a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Psionic Focus
entries: By 10th level, you attain a profound understanding of the fundamentals of psionics, improving your ability to focus, both psychically and in {@status concentration||concentration}. You are now able to use your psychic focus feature while you have no psi points available. In addition, if you fail a Constitution saving throw in order to not lose {@status {@status concentration||concentration}|phb|{@status concentration||concentration}} and you have a psychic focus active, you can end your psychic focus to reroll the saving throw, potentially turning the failure into a success.

classFeature.name: Psionic Mastery
entries: Beginning at 11th level, your mastery of psionic energy allows you to push your mind beyond its normal limits. As an action, you gain 9 mastery points that can be spent like psi points on disciplines that require an action or a bonus action to use. You can use all 9 points on one discipline, or you can spread them across multiple disciplines. You can’t also spend both psi points and mastery points on the same discipline. If you have features that allow you to spend psi points to alter the effectiveness of your disciplines such as Wu Jen's Metamagic feature or Awakened's Psionic Surge feature, you may distribute mastery points into those features. When you finish a long rest, you lose any mastery points that you haven’t spent.

If more than one of the disciplines you activate with mastery points require {@status {@status concentration||concentration}|phb|{@status concentration||concentration}}, you can concentrate on all of them. Activating one of them ends any effect you were already concentrating on, and if you begin concentrating on an effect that doesn’t use these mastery points, the disciplines that you’re concentrating on end.

The pool of psi points you gain from this feature increases as you gain levels in this class. At 13th level, the pool increases to 10. At 15th level, the pool increases to 11. At 17th level, the pool increases to 13.
You have one use of this feature, and you regain any expended use of it with a long rest. You gain one additional use of this feature at 13th, 15th, and 17th level.

classFeature.name: Feat
entries: When you reach 12th level, you gain a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Psionic Order feature
entries: At 14th level, you gain a feature from your Psionic Order.

classFeature.name: Feat
entries: When you reach 16th level, you gain a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Strength of Mind
entries: Starting at 18th level, your mastery of psionics allows you to augment your defenses. Whenever you finish a short or long rest, you can choose to gain proficiency in a saving throw that you lack proficiency in. This benefit lasts until your next short or long rest.

classFeature.name: Feat
entries: When you reach 19th level, you gain a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Psionic Body
entries: At 20th level, your mastery of psionic power causes your mind to transcend the body. Your physical form is infused with psionic energy. You gain the following benefits:

items: You suffer none of the frailty of old age, and you can't be aged magically. You can still die of old age, however.
You gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, poison, and slashing damage.
You have advantage on all saving throws against being Diseased, {@condition Petrified|phb}, or {@condition Poisoned|phb}.
You can use an action to expend 1 psi point to end one effect on yourself that is causing you to be Diseased, {@condition Petrified|phb}, or {@condition Poisoned|phb}.

If you die from anything other than old age, roll a DC 30 Intelligence saving throw. On a success, instead of dying, you discorporate with 0 hit points and you fall unconscious. You and any objects being worn or carried by you disappear. You appear at a spot of your choice {@dice 1d3} days later on the plane of existence where you died, suffering {@dice 2d4+1} Tiers of Bestir {@condition Exhaustion|THICC} and gaining 1 hit point.

subclassFeature.name: Order of the Avatar
entries: Psions of the Order of the Avatar delve into the world of emotion, mastering their inner life to such an extent that they can manipulate and amplify the emotions of others with the same ease that an artist shapes clay. Known as Avatars, these psions vary from tyrants to inspiring leaders who are loved by their followers. Avatars can bring out extreme emotions in the people around them. For their allies, they can lend hope, ferocity, and courage, transforming a fighting band into a deadly, unified force. For their enemies, they bring fear, disgust, and trepidation that can make even the most hardened veteran act like a shaky rookie.

subclassFeature.name: Required Discipline
entries: The first discipline you know must be chosen from among the {@filter Avatar Disciplines|optionalfeatures|feature type=AVD}.

subclassFeature.name: Armor Training
entries: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with light armor, medium armor, light shields, and medium shields.

subclassFeature.name: Influential Presence
entries: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with two of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Animal Handling}, {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Performance}, and {@skill Persuasion}.

subclassFeature.name: Avatar of Emotion
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you project an aura of confidence, leading allies to follow you and enemies to waver in front of you. While you aren’t {@condition Incapacitated|phb}, any ally within 30 feet of you who can see you have a bonus to saving throws against being {@condition Charmed|phb}, {@condition Frightened|phb}, or {@condition Frenzied|THICC} equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 0).
As a reaction to when a creature in the aura other than yourself makes an ability check, you may spend a psi point to increase or decrease the result of the roll by {@dice 2d2-1}.

subclassFeature.name: Avatar of Battle
entries: Starting at 6th level, you project an inspiring aura. While you aren’t {@condition Incapacitated|phb}, each ally within 30 feet of you who can see you gains a bonus to initiative rolls equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 0).
As a reaction to when a creature in the aura other than yourself makes an attack roll, you may spend a psi point to increase or decrease the result of the roll by {@dice 2d2-1}.

subclassFeature.name: Psionic Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon attacks with psychic energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon, you can deal an extra {@dice 1d8} psychic damage to that target. When you reach 14th level, this extra damage increases to {@dice 2d8}.

subclassFeature.name: Avatar of Protection
entries: Beginning at 14th level, you project an aura of resilience. While you aren’t {@condition Incapacitated|phb}, each ally within 30 feet of you who can see you gains additional temporary hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 0) whenever they regain hit points or temporary hit points from a psionic discipline.

As a reaction to when a creature in the aura other than yourself makes a saving throw, you may spend a psi point to increase or decrease the result of the roll by {@dice 2d2-1}. If you are spending this point on a target of a saving throw against a discipline that you used this turn, you treat the psi point dedicated to this feature as a part of the psi points dedicated to the discipline for the purposes of determining whether or not you are exceeding your psi limit.

subclassFeature.name: Order of the Awakened
entries: Psions dedicated to the Order of the Awakened seek to unlock the full potential of the mind. By transcending the physical, the Awakened hope to attain a state of being focused on pure intellect and mental energy. The Awakened are skilled at bending minds and unleashing devastating psionic attacks, and they can read the secrets of the world through psionic energy. Awakened psions who take to adventuring excel at unraveling mysteries, solving puzzles, and defeating monsters by turning them into unwilling pawns.

subclassFeature.name: Required Discipline
entries: The first discipline you know must be chosen from among the {@filter Awakened Disciplines|optionalfeatures|feature type=AWD}.

subclassFeature.name: Awakened Talent
entries: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with two of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Perception}, and {@skill Persuasion}. Then, choose two skills from that list that you have proficiency in, and gain expertise in those skills.

subclassFeature.name: Psionic Investigation
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can focus your mind to read the psionic imprint left on an object. If you hold an object and concentrate on it for 10 minutes (as if concentrating on a psionic discipline), you learn a few basic facts about it. You gain a mental image from the object’s point of view, showing the last creature to hold the object within the past 24 hours. You also learn of any events that have occurred within 20 feet of the object within the past hour. The events you perceive unfold from the object’s perspective. You see and hear such events as if you were there, but can’t use other senses.

Additionally, you can spend 2 psi points to embed an intangible psionic sensor within the object. For the next 24 hours, you can use an action to learn the object’s location relative to you (its distance and direction) and to look at the object’s surroundings from its point of view as if you were there. This perception lasts until the start of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest or spend 1 psi point to use this feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Psionic Surge
entries: Starting at 6th level, you can overload yourself to batter down an opponent’s defenses. You can spend 2 psi points to impose disadvantage on a single target’s saving throw against a discipline or talent you use. You can use this feature multiple times on different targets if a given discipline or talent targets multiple creatures. You can’t spend these points if doing so would increase the discipline’s cost above your psi limit.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Psionics
entries: At 8th level, you add your Intelligence modifier to any damage roll you make for a psionic talent.

subclassFeature.name: Spectral Form
entries: At 14th level, you gain the ability to become a ghostly figure of psionic energy. As an action, you can transform into a transparent, ghostly version of yourself. While in this form, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have resistance to all nonmagical damage.
You gain the benefits of the {@spell Hush|COOMS} and {@spell Transparency|COOMS} spells, as if they were cast on you.
You can spend 5 feet of movement to automatically escape any restraint, such as manacles, rope, chain, or a creature that has you {@condition Grappled|phb}.
You can pass through objects and creatures while moving but can't willingly end your movement in their spaces.

entries: This form lasts for 10 minutes or until you use an action to end it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest or spend 7 psi points to use this feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Order of the Immortal
entries: The Order of the Immortal uses psionic energy to augment and modify the physical form. Followers of this order are known as Immortals. They use psionic energy to modify their bodies, strengthening them against attack and turning themselves into living weapons. Their mastery of the physical form grants them their name, for Immortals are notoriously difficult to kill.

subclassFeature.name: Required Discipline
entries: The first discipline you know must be chosen from among the {@filter Immortal Disciplines|optionalfeatures|feature type=ID}.

subclassFeature.name: Immortal Durability
entries: Starting at 1st level, your hit point maximum increases by 1 and it increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level in this class. In addition, while you aren’t wearing armor, your base AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Immortal Sustenance
entries: At 1st level, your psionic energy becomes enough to sustain yourself. You can spend 1 psi point over the course of 10 minutes spent as if in {@status concentration||concentration} in order to gain the effects of eating and drinking for the day, as you use your psionic powers to fuel your physical form.

subclassFeature.name: Psionic Resilience
entries: Starting at 3rd level, your psionic energy grants you extraordinary fortitude. As an action, while you have a psychic focus active, you can give yourself temporary hit points equal to your psion level plus your Intelligence modifier. These temporary hit points last until your psychic focus ends.

subclassFeature.name: Mental Dampening
entries: Starting at 6th level, your psionic fortitude allows you to reduce the damage of even the harshest of blows towards you. As a reaction when you take damage from a source you can see, you can halve that damage against you. You can use this reaction a number of times per short or long rest equal to your Intelligence modifier. While you have no uses available, you can spend 3 psi points to use this feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Psionic Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon attacks with psychic energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon, you can deal an extra {@dice 1d8} psychic damage to that target. When you reach 14th level, this extra damage increases to {@dice 2d8}.

subclassFeature.name: Surge of Health
entries: Starting at 14th level, you can draw on your reserves of psionic power to survive beyond death. At the end of your turn while at 0 hit points, you can spend 5 psi points to immediately regain a number of hit points equal to your psion level + your Intelligence modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Order of the Nomad
entries: Psions of the Order of the Nomad keep their minds in a strange, rarified state. They seek to accumulate as much knowledge as possible, as they quest to unravel the mysteries of the multiverse and seek the underlying structure of all things. At the same time, they perceive a bizarre, living web of knowledge they call the noosphere. Nomads, as their name indicates, delight in travel, exploration, and discovery. They desire to accumulate as much knowledge as possible, and the pursuit of secrets and hidden lore can become an obsession for them.

subclassFeature.name: Required Discipline
entries: The first discipline you know must be chosen from among the {@filter Nomad Disciplines|optionalfeatures|feature type=ND}.

subclassFeature.name: Armor Proficiency
entries: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with light armor.

subclassFeature.name: Nomadic Travel
entries: At 1st level, you learn how to psionically bolster travelling the world, granting you the following benefits:

items: You can spend 1 psi point to take the {@action Hide} action as a bonus action.

While you have a psychic focus active, you ignore {@quickref difficult terrain||3} and have advantage on {@skill Athletics} checks related to the {@action Climb|THICC} and {@action Swim|THICC} actions.
Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger.
If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.
When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would.
While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area.

subclassFeature.name: Breadth of Knowledge
entries: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to extend your knowledge. Once per long rest, you may meditate for 10 minutes as if in {@status concentration||concentration}. At the end of this meditation, you gain proficiency in a skill, tool, vehicle, language, weapon, instrument, or gaming set of your choice. Someone on your plane of existence must be proficient in your choice in order to gain this bonus. This proficiency lasts until your next long rest, or until you spend 1 psi point to meditate in the same way to replace it with a different proficiency from the list.

subclassFeature.name: Memory of One Thousand Steps
entries: At 6th, you gain the ability to use psionics to recall your steps. As a reaction when you are hit by an attack, you can teleport to an unoccupied space that you occupied since the last time you started your turn, causing the attack to miss you if it does not also target that space. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you spend 5 psi points or finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Psionic Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon attacks with psychic energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon, you can deal an extra {@dice 1d8} psychic damage to that target. When you reach 14th level, this extra damage increases to {@dice 2d8}.

subclassFeature.name: Hastened Journey
entries: At 14th level, your mind can mystically move your body with ease. Once on each of your turns, you can forfeit an amount of your movement up to your walking speed to teleport the distance you forfeited. You must teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you regain all expended uses of this feature on a short or long rest. Alternatively, you can spend 1 psi point to use this feature when it has no uses remaining.

subclassFeature.name: Order of the Soulknife
entries: The Order of the Soulknife sacrifices the breadth of knowledge other psions gain to focus on a specific psionic technique. These psions learn to manifest a deadly weapon of pure psychic energy that they can use to cleave through foes. Soul knives vary widely in their approach to this path. Some follow it out of a desire to achieve martial perfection. Others are ruthless assassins who seek to become the perfect killer.

subclassFeature.name: Required Discipline
entries: The first discipline you know must be chosen from among the {@filter Soulknife Disciplines|optionalfeatures|feature type=SD}.

subclassFeature.name: Armor Training
entries: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with light armor and parrying shields.

subclassFeature.name: Psychic Blades
entries: Starting at 1st level, you can manifest your psionic power as shimmering blades of psychic energy. Whenever you take the Attack action, you can manifest a psychic blade from your free hand and make the attack with that blade. This magic blade is a simple melee weapon with the finesse and thrown properties. It has a normal range of 60 feet and no long range, and on a hit, it deals psychic damage equal to {@dice 1d6} plus the ability modifier you used for the attack roll. The blade vanishes immediately after it hits or misses its target, and it leaves no mark on its target if it deals damage.

After you attack with the blade, you can make a melee or ranged weapon attack with a second psychic blade as a bonus action on the same turn, provided your other hand is free to create it. The damage die of this bonus attack is {@dice 1d4}, instead of {@dice 1d6}, and it otherwise follows the standard rules for dual weapon fighting.

subclassFeature.name: Hone the Blade
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can spend psi points up to your psi limit to augment your soulknives' attack rolls and damage. You gain a bonus to attack and damage rolls with your soulknives depending on the number of psi points spent, as shown on the table below. This bonus lasts for 10 minutes, or until you use this feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Enhanced Blade
entries: Starting at 6th level, when you use Hone the Blade, you can choose an additional benefit to gain for the duration of the ability from the following list:

items: You gain additional AC equal to the bonus granted by Hone the Blade.
Your attacks with your psychic blades score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.
You can choose to reroll any attack roll you make with the psychic blades up to a number of times equal to twice the bonus granted by Hone the Blade, but you must use the new roll when you do so.
Once per turn when you hit a creature with your psychic blades, you regain hit points equal to the bonus granted by Hone the Blade.

Once per turn when you hit a creature with your psychic blades, you can choose to deal an extra number of {@dice d8} damage to the target equal to the bonus granted by Hone the Blade, but you suffer the same number of {@dice d4} psychic damage.

When you score a critical hit with your psychic blades, the target suffers a penalty to their Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma ability scores (distributed at your discretion) equal to the bonus granted by Hone the Blade.

subclassFeature.name: Psionic Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon attacks with psychic energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon, you can deal an extra {@dice 1d8} psychic damage to that target. When you reach 14th level, this extra damage increases to {@dice 2d8}.

subclassFeature.name: Psionic Flurry
entries: Starting at 14th level, you can overload yourself to speed up your attacks. You may spend 5 psi points as an action to make one attack against any number of creatures within 5 feet of you with advantage.

subclassFeature.name: Order of the Wu Jen
entries: The Order of the Wu Jen features some of the most devoted psions. These psions seek to lock themselves away from the world, denying the limits of the physical world and replacing it with a reality that they create for themselves. Known as wu jens, these psions cast their minds into the world, seize control of its fundamental principles, and rebuild it. In practical terms, wu jens excel at controlling the forces of the natural world. They can hurl objects with their minds, control the four elements, and alter reality to fit their desires.

subclassFeature.name: Required Discipline
entries: The first discipline you know must be chosen from among the {@filter Wu Jen Disciplines|optionalfeatures|feature type=WJD}.

subclassFeature.name: Hermit's Study
entries: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with two of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Animal Handling}, {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Medicine}, {@skill Nature}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Religion}, or {@skill Survival}. Additionally, you gain proficiency with one tool or language of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Metamagic
entries: At 3rd level, your deepened knowledge with the world allows you to have greater control over your psionics. You learn two {@filter Metamagic options|optionalfeatures|feature type=MM} of your choice from the sorcerer class. You use psi points in place of sorcery points, and you use them on discipline abilities rather than spells. You can use only one Metamagic option on a discipline when you manifest one of its effects, unless the option says otherwise. You can’t use a metamagic option on a discipline if doing so would increase the discipline’s cost above your psi limit. Whenever you reach a level that grants the Feat feature, you can replace one of these Metamagic options with another one from the sorcerer class.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Attunement
entries: Starting at 6th level, when a creature’s resistance reduces the damage dealt by a psionic discipline of yours, you can spend 1 psi point to cause that use of the discipline to ignore the creature’s resistance. You can’t spend this point if doing so would increase the discipline’s cost above your psi limit.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Psionics
entries: At 8th level, you add your Intelligence modifier to any damage roll you make for a psionic talent.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Mastery
entries: Starting at 14th level, if you have resistance to a type of damage (including damage reduction) you can spend 2 psi points as a reaction when you take damage of that type to ignore that damage and gain immunity to that damage type until the end of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Beacon
entries: As a bonus action, you cause bright light to radiate from your body in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like. The light lasts for 1 hour, and you can extinguish it earlier as a bonus action.

optionalfeature.name: Blade Meld
entries: As a bonus action, a one-handed melee weapon you hold becomes one with your hand. For the next minute, you can’t let go of the weapon nor can it be forced from your grasp.

optionalfeature.name: Blind Spot
entries: As a bonus action, you erase your image from the mind of one creature you can see within 120 feet of you; the target must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw, or you are {@condition Invisible|phb} to it until the end of your next turn. On a success, the creature is immune to the effects of this talent for 24 hours.

optionalfeature.name: Delusion
entries: As a bonus action, you plant a false belief in the mind of one creature that you can see within 60 feet of you. The target must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a success, the creature experiences déjà vu. On a failure, you can create a sound or an image. Only the target of this talent perceives the sound or image you create.

If you create a sound, its volume can range from a whisper to a scream. It can be your voice, someone else's voice, a creature's roar, a musical instrument, or any other sound you pick. It lasts for 1 minute.

If you create an object, it must fit within a 5- foot cube and can’t move or be reflective. The image can't create any effect that influences a sense other than sight. The image lasts for 1 minute, and it disappears if the creature touches it.

optionalfeature.name: Disorient
entries: You drive a disorienting spike of psychic energy into the mind of one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The target must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw or take {@dice 1d6} psychic damage and subtract {@dice 1d4} from the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn. Additionally, the creature loses its bearings. If the creature cannot tell which way it is going, (for example, if it is {@condition Blinded|phb}), the creature moves in a random direction next turn if it decides to move until it regains its orientation.
This talent's damage increases by {@dice 1d6} when you reach certain levels: 5th level ({@dice 2d6}), 11th level ({@dice 3d6}), and 17th level ({@dice 4d6}).

optionalfeature.name: Energy Beam
entries: As an action, you make a ranged spell attack against one target you can see within 90 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes {@dice 1d8} acid, fire, or lightning damage (your choice).
The talent’s damage increases by {@dice 1d8} when you reach 5th level ({@dice 2d8}), 11th level ({@dice 3d8}), and 17th level ({@dice 4d8}).

optionalfeature.name: Energy Blast
entries: As an action, you target one creature you can see within 90 feet of you. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take {@dice 1d8} cold, fire, or thunder damage (your choice). The sound of the blast can be heard up to 60 feet away.
The talent’s damage increases by {@dice 1d8} when you reach 5th level ({@dice 2d8}), 11th level ({@dice 3d8}), and 17th level ({@dice 4d8}).

optionalfeature.name: Hone Weapon
entries: As a bonus action, you imbue a simple melee weapon with psionic power for one minute. While affected this way, you may use intelligence instead of strength for attacks with this weapon, the weapon’s damage die becomes a {@dice d8}, and is considered magical if it is not already.

To use this on the Psychic Blades feature of the Soulknife subclass, you must have at least one empty hand to temporarily manifest a blade while you use this talent. While this affects the Soulknife, it affects any blade manifested with that feature for 1 minute.

optionalfeature.name: Light Step
entries: As a bonus action, you alter your density and weight to improve your mobility. For the rest of your turn, your walking speed increases by 10 feet, and the first time you stand up this turn, you do so without expending any of your movement if your speed is greater than 0.

optionalfeature.name: Mind Meld
entries: As a bonus action, you can communicate telepathically with one willing creature you can see within 120 feet of you. The target must have an Intelligence of at least 2, otherwise this talent fails and the bonus action is wasted. This communication can occur until the end of the current turn. You don’t need to share a language with the target for it to understand your telepathic utterances, and it understands you even if it lacks a language. You also can gain access to one six-second fragment of a memory of the target’s choice if they are willing, gaining the target’s recollection of one thing it saw or did. Alternatively, you can share a mental image with the target that you are able to visualize or a six-second fragment of a memory of yours.

optionalfeature.name: Mind Thrust
entries: As an action, you target one creature you can see within 120 feet of you. The target must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw or take {@dice 1d10} psychic damage.
The talent’s damage increases by {@dice 1d10} when you reach 5th level ({@dice 2d10}), 11th level ({@dice 3d10}), and 17th level ({@dice 4d10}).

optionalfeature.name: Minor Aerokinesis
entries: As a bonus action, you seize the air and compel it to create one of the following effects at a point you can see within 30 feet of yourself:

items: One Medium or smaller creature that you choose must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 5 feet away from you.

You create a small blast of air capable of moving one object that is neither held nor carried and that weighs no more than 5 pounds. The object is pushed up to 10 feet away from you. It isn't pushed with enough force to cause damage.
You create a harmless sensory effect using air, such as causing leaves to rustle, wind to slam shutters closed, or your clothing to ripple in a breeze.
You can gently control the direction of airflow in a 5-foot cube, not enough to cause damage or blow away a {@spell Fog Cloud}.

entries: The talent's range increases by 30 feet when you reach 5th level (60 feet), 11th level (90 feet), and 17th level (120 feet).

optionalfeature.name: Minor Hydrokinesis
entries: As a bonus action, choose an area of water that you can see within 30 feet of yourself and that fits within a 5-foot cube. You manipulate it in one of the following ways:

items: You instantaneously move or otherwise change the flow of the water as you direct, up to 5 feet in any direction. This movement doesn't have enough force to cause damage.
You cause the water to form into simple shapes and animate at your direction. This change lasts for 1 hour.
You change the water's color or opacity. The water must be changed in the same way throughout. This change lasts for 1 hour.
You freeze the water, provided that there are no creatures in it. The water unfreezes in 1 hour.

entries: If you manifest this talent multiple times, you can have no more than three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time, and you can dismiss such an effect as a bonus action.
The talent's range increases by 30 feet when you reach 5th level (60 feet), 11th level (90 feet), and 17th level (120 feet).

optionalfeature.name: Minor Hypnosis
entries: As an action, when you make an ability check to interact socially with a creature you can see within 30 feet of you, you can attempt to psychically beguile them. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against being {@condition Charmed|phb}. On a failure, you have advantage on the ability check towards that creature. On a success, you have disadvantage on the roll, as the creature knows you attempted to charm it, and the creature is immune to the effects of this talent for 24 hours.

optionalfeature.name: Minor Pyrokinesis
entries: As a bonus action, choose nonmagical flame that you can see within 30 feet of yourself and that fits within a 5-foot cube. You affect it in one of the following ways:

items: You instantaneously expand the flame 5 feet in one direction, provided that wood or other fuel is present in the new location.
You instantaneously extinguish the flames within the cube.
You double or halve the area of bright light and dim light cast by the flame, change its color, or both. The change lasts for 1 hour.
You cause simple shapes such as the vague form of a creature, an inanimate object, or a location to appear within the flames and animate as you like. The shapes last for 1 hour.

entries: If you manifest this talent multiple times, you can have up to three non-instantaneous effects created by it active at a time, and you can dismiss such an effect as a bonus action.
The talent's range increases by 30 feet when you reach 5th level (60 feet), 11th level (90 feet), and 17th level (120 feet).

optionalfeature.name: Minor Telekinesis
entries: You can use your action to manipulate or move one object within 30 feet of you. The object can’t weigh more than 10 pounds, and you can’t affect an object being worn or carried by another creature. If the object is loose, you can move it up to 30 feet in any direction. This talent allows you to open an unlocked door, pour out a beer stein, and so on. The object falls to the ground at the start of your next turn if you leave it suspended in midair and choose to not immediately use your action to use this talent.

optionalfeature.name: Minor Terrakinesis
entries: As a bonus action, choose a portion of dirt or stone that you can see within 30 feet of yourself and that fits within a 5-foot cube. You manipulate it in one of the following ways:

items: If you target an area of loose earth in an unoccupied space such as dirt, sand, silt, gravel, or clay, you can instantaneously excavate it, move it along the ground, and deposit it up to 5 feet away. This movement doesn't involve enough force to cause damage.

If you target an area of loose earth in an unoccupied space such as dirt, sand, silt, gravel, or clay, you can shape it to whatever form you desire, which it will retain for 1 hour. The individual pieces of loose earth that comprise the desired form must be touching, and are still affected by gravity. If the structure you create receives any damage, this effect ends.
You cause shapes, colors, or both to form in the dirt or stone, spelling out words, creating images, or shaping patterns within the existing design of the medium. The changes last for 1 hour.

If the dirt or stone you target is on the ground, you cause it to become difficult terrain. Alternatively, you can cause the ground to become normal terrain if it is already difficult terrain. This change lasts for 1 hour.

entries: If you manifest this talent multiple times, you can have no more than three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time, and you can dismiss such an effect as a bonus action.
The talent's range increases by 30 feet when you reach 5th level (60 feet), 11th level (90 feet), and 17th level (120 feet).

optionalfeature.name: Telekinetic Slam
entries: As an action, you try to grasp one creature you can see within 60 feet of you, with a hand crafted from telekinetic energy. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or take 1d4 force damage. If it takes any of this damage and is Large or smaller, you can shove it 5 feet in a straight line in a direction of your choice. You can’t lift the target off the ground unless it is already airborne or underwater. Alternatively, if the creature is within 10 feet of you and grounded, you can instead choose to shove it Prone.
The talent’s damage increases by {@dice 1d4} when you reach 5th level ({@dice 2d4}), 11th level ({@dice 3d4}), and 17th level ({@dice 4d4}).

optionalfeature.name: Adaptive Body
entries: {@i Immortal Discipline}
You can alter your body to match your surroundings, allowing you to withstand punishing environments. With greater psi energy, you can extend this protection to others.

items: {@b Psychic Focus.} While focused on this discipline, you can exist comfortably in conditions between -50 and 140 degrees Fahrenheit. On top of this, any cold or fire damage you take is reduced by 2.

{@b Environmental Adaptation (1—7 psi)} As an action, you or a creature you touch ignores the effects of extreme heat or cold for the next hour. On top of this, any acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage the creature takes is reduced by an amount equal to the psi points spent.

{@b Adaptive Shield (2 psi)} When you take acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to gain resistance to damage of that type—including the triggering damage— until the end of your next turn.
{@b Enhanced Immunity (3 psi)} As an action, you touch one creature and grant it resistance to poison damage and advantage on all saving throws against being poisoned or diseased for 1 hour.

{@b Energy Adaptation (5 psi; conc., 1 hr.)} As an action, you can touch one creature and give it resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage (your choice), which lasts until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends.

{@b Energy Immunity (7 psi; conc., 1 min.)} As an action, you gain immunity to acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage (your choice), which lasts until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends.

optionalfeature.name: Aerokinesis
entries: {@i Wu Jen Discipline}
You become one with the power of elemental air.

items: {@b Psychic Focus.} While focused on this discipline, when you fall, you can use a reaction to cause air to push against your fall, slowing your descent to only fall 60 feet per round until you land. When you land, you take no damage from the fall and can choose to land on your feet.

{@b Wind Step (1—7 psi)} As part of your move on your turn, you can fly up to 20 feet for each psi point spent. You can not fly more than you have movement speed remaining this turn. If you end this flight in the air, you fall unless something else holds you aloft.

{@b Wind Stream (1—7 psi)} As an action, you create a line of focused air that is 30 feet long and 5 feet wide. Each creature in that area must make a Strength saving throw, taking 1d4 bludgeoning damage per psi point spent and being knocked prone on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The wind disperses gas or vapor, and it extinguishes candles, torches, and similar unprotected flames in the area. It causes protected flames, such as those of lanterns, to dance wildly and has a 50 percent chance to extinguish them.

{@b Cloak of Wind (3 psi; conc., 10 min.)} As a bonus action, you seize control of the air around you to create a protective veil. Until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends, weapon attack rolls against you made by a creature further than 5 feet away have disadvantage, and when a creature you can see misses you with a ranged weapon attack, you can use your reaction to make a ranged spell attack against one creature within 30 feet of you as you throw the projectile away from yourself. On a hit, the target takes the damage that would have taken.

{@b Whirlwind (3 psi)} As an action, choose a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Winds howl in a 15-foot-radius sphere centered on that point. Each creature in the sphere must succeed on a Strength saving throw or take {@dice 1d6} bludgeoning damage and be moved 10 feet in any direction to an unoccupied space of your choice in the sphere. Creatures that succeed the saving throw instead take half damage and are not moved. Any loose object in the sphere is moved 10 feet to an unoccupied space of your choice within it if the object weighs no more than 100 pounds. The objects are not flung with enough force to deal damage.
{@b Wind Form (5 psi; conc., 10 min.)} As a bonus action, you gain a hovering speed of 60 feet, which lasts until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends.

{@b Misty Form (6 psi; conc., 1 min.)} As an action, your body becomes like a misty cloud until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends. In this form, you gain resistance to damage from nonmagical weapons, and you can’t take actions other than the {@action Dash} action. You can pass through openings that are no more than 1 inch wide without squeezing.

{@b Animate Air (7 psi; conc., 1 hr.)} As an action, you cause an air elemental to appear in an unoccupied space filled with air that you can see within 120 feet of you. The elemental lasts until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends, and it obeys your verbal commands. In combat, roll for its initiative, and choose its behavior during its turns. When this effect ends, the elemental disappears. The DM has their stat block.

optionalfeature.name: Animation
entries: {@i Avatar Discipline}
You can use your psionic powers to bestow life and sentience onto objects and creatures.

items: {@b Psychic Focus.} While focused on this discipline, you add {@dice 1d4} to the result of any Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks made by you.

{@b Don (1 psi)} As an action, you briefly animate a set of wearable equipment that fits you and is not currently being worn, such as a backpack, quiver, or shield, and/or any armor within range. The equipment quickly slots itself onto you where it should be, fastened and ready for use if you can equip it.

{@b Doff (1 psi)} As an action, you briefly animate a set of equipment that you are wearing, such as a backpack, quiver, or shield, and/or any armor within range. The equipment quickly disrobes off of you, folding up into a backpack if it would fit and one is available. Otherwise, the equipment folds itself neatly beside you.

{@b Dictate (1—7 psi)} As an action, you verbally designate the writing implement and surface(s) to write on that both fit within a 5-foot cube along with the names of a number of creatures within 60 feet per psi point spent. For the duration, the writing implement animates and writes down anything said by the creatures while they are within 60 feet of the surface that is being written down on. The writing implement specifies who says what by writing the name assigned to them before what they say whenever the speaker switches. If two or more creatures talk over each other, the writing implement will prioritize creatures in the order that their names were stated. The writing implement may be ink and quill, blood and a pen, or a dagger, to list some examples. If you choose a combination of writing implement and surface that would be difficult or impossible to write upon, such as a chisel and a stone slab, the feature fails.

{@b Animate Weapon (2—7 psi; conc., 1 min.)} As an action, you touch a weapon or shield that is not being held or worn by any other creature, momentarily bringing it to life. You can target another item per additional psi point spent. It acts as a {@creature Flying Sword|MM} (see its stat block), but the longsword is replaced with the chosen item, their antimagic susceptibility is replaced with antipsionic susceptibility, and their Constitution is replaced with your Intelligence score. Additionally, their attack (if they have one) uses your discipline attack modifier for its attack and damage rolls. If the chosen item was a weapon, it is able to make use of its versatile and double properties while fighting. For example, a versatile weapon will always use the versatile damage, and a double weapon will be able to attack twice. If the chosen item was a shield, it gains the AC and parrying capabilities of the shield, and will knock itself wide open when it attacks. As a bonus action, you can mentally command the creature if it is within 90 feet of you. (If you control multiple creatures with this feature, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one.) You decide what action the creature will take and where they will move during their next turn, or you can issue a general command, such as to guard a chamber or passageway against your foes. If you issue no commands, the creatures do nothing except defend themselves against hostile creatures. Once given an order, the creatures continue to follow it until their task is complete. If the item reaches 0 hit points, it receives a -1 penalty for every 10 excess damage it receives, potentially breaking it. Adamantine items only suffer this potential penalty when struck by an adamantine weapon. The feature ends early if the item breaks or if your {@status concentration||concentration} ends.

{@b Animate Armor (3—7 psi; conc., 1 min.)} As an action, you touch a full suit of armor, such as any heavy armor or scale mail, that is not currently being worn, temporarily bringing it to life. You can target another item per additional psi point spent. It acts as an {@creature Animated Armor|MM} (see its stat block), but the AC is replaced with that of the chosen item, their antimagic susceptibility is replaced with antipsionic susceptibility, and their Constitution is replaced with your Intelligence score. Additionally, their Slam attack uses your discipline attack modifier for its attack and damage rolls. As a bonus action, you can mentally command the creature if it is within 90 feet of you. (If you control multiple creatures with this feature, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one.) You decide what action the creature will take and where they will move during their next turn, or you can issue a general command, such as to guard a chamber or passageway against your foes. If you issue no commands, the creatures do nothing except defend themselves against hostile creatures. Once given an order, the creatures continue to follow it until their task is complete. If the armor reaches 0 hit points, it receives a -1 penalty for every 10 excess damage it receives, potentially breaking it. Adamantine items only suffer this potential penalty when struck by an adamantine weapon. The feature ends early if the item breaks or if your {@status concentration||concentration} ends.

{@b Animate Tiny Servant (5—7 psi)} You touch one Tiny, nonmagical object that isn't attached to another object or a surface and isn't being carried by another creature. You can target another suit of armor per additional psi point spent. You can create two more Tiny Servants per additional psi point spent. The target animates and sprouts little arms and legs, becoming a creature under your control until 8 hours pass or the creature drops to 0 hit points. See the stat block for its statistics. As a bonus action, you can mentally command the creature if it is within 120 feet of you. (If you control multiple creatures with this feature, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one.) You decide what action the creature will take and where it will move during its next turn, or you can issue a simple, general command, such as to fetch a key, stand watch, or stack some books. If you issue no commands, the servant does nothing other than defend itself against hostile creatures. Once given an order, the servant continues to follow that order until its task is complete. When the creature drops to 0 hit points, it reverts to its original form, and any remaining damage carries over to that form.

{@b Animate Objects (7 psi; conc., 1 min.)} As an action, objects come to life at your command. Choose up to ten nonmagical objects within range that are not being worn or carried. Medium targets count as two objects, Large targets count as four objects, Huge targets count as eight objects. You can't animate any object larger than Huge. Each target animates and becomes a creature under your control until you lose {@status concentration||concentration} or until it is reduced to 0 hit points. As a bonus action, you can mentally command any creature you made with this feature if the creature is within 500 feet of you (if you control multiple creatures, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one). You decide what action the creature will take and where it will move during its next turn, or you can issue a general command, such as to guard a particular chamber or corridor. If you issue no commands, the creature only defends itself against hostile creatures. Once given an order, the creature continues to follow it until its task is complete.

An animated object is a construct with AC, hit points, attacks, Strength, and Dexterity determined by its size. Its Constitution is 10 and its Intelligence and Wisdom are 3, and its Charisma is 1. Its speed is 30 feet; if the object lacks legs or other appendages it can use for locomotion, it instead has a flying speed of 30 feet and can hover. If the object is securely attached to a surface or a larger object, such as a chain bolted to a wall, its speed is 0. It has {@sense blindsight} with a radius of 30 feet and is blind beyond that distance. When the animated object drops to 0 hit points, it reverts to its original object form, and any remaining damage carries over to its original object form. If you command an object to attack, it can make a single melee attack against a creature within 5 feet of it. It makes a slam attack with an attack bonus and bludgeoning damage determined by its size. The DM might rule that a specific object inflicts slashing or piercing damage based on its form.

{@b Awaken (7 psi)} Over the course of 8 hours, as if in {@status concentration||concentration}, you attempt to impart your sapience into a Huge or smaller beast or plant that has either no Intelligence score or an Intelligence of 3 or less. If you two become separated by more than 5 feet or you lose your {@status concentration||concentration} during the 8 hours for any reason, or if the creature has an Intelligence of 4 or more, the feature fails but the psi points are not wasted. You transfer points from your Intelligence score until the target reaches 10 Intelligence. If this would put your Intelligence score below 4, the feature fails and the psi points are wasted. Otherwise, the target gains the ability to speak one language you know. The target additionally gains your personality traits, ideals, bonds, and flaws. If the target is a plant, it gains the ability to move its limbs, roots, vines, creepers, and so forth, and it gains senses similar to a human's. Your DM chooses statistics appropriate for the awakened plant, such as the statistics for the {@creature awakened shrub|MM} or the {@creature awakened tree|MM}. The awakened beast or plant is {@condition Charmed} by you for 30 days or until you or your companions do anything harmful to it. When the {@condition Charmed} condition ends, the awakened creature chooses whether to remain friendly to you, based on how you treated it while it was {@condition Charmed}. It will additionally modify its personality traits, ideals, bonds, and flaws based on its experiences during this time. At the end of every long rest, until you have regained every transferred point of Intelligence, you are able to make an Intelligence saving throw. The DC of the saving throw is 40 minus the amount of days that have passed. You regain one point of Intelligence on a success. The awakened creature does not lose the point of Intelligence when you regain it.

optionalfeature.name: Atmokinesis
entries: {@i Wu Jen Discipline}
Your mind reaches into the sky, reshaping the stuff of storms to serve your needs.

items: {@b Psychic Focus.} While focused on this discipline, any thunder damage you take is reduced by 3.

{@b Cloud Steps (1—7 psi; conc., 10 min.)} As an action, you conjure forth clouds to create a solid, translucent staircase within 60 feet of you that lasts until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends. The stairs form a spiral that fills a cylinder with a 5 foot radius that reaches upward 10 feet per psi point spent. If the stairs are created underneath yourself, you can decide to have the stairs immediately carry you to the stop as the staircase is being constructed.

{@b Thunderstrike (1—7 psi)} As an action, you encase your fist in thunderous energy before making a melee spell attack against one creature in your reach. On a hit, you deal {@dice 2d8} thunder damage per psi point spent. Additionally, the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 5 feet away from you per psi point spent and knocked {@condition Prone}.

{@b Wall of Clouds (2 psi; conc., 10 min.)} As an action, you create a wall of clouds, at least one portion of which must be within 60 feet of you. The wall is 60 feet long, 15 feet high, and 1 foot thick. The wall lasts until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends. Creatures can pass through it without hindrance, but the wall blocks vision.

{@b Deafening Crack (5—7 psi)} As an action, choose a point you can see within 60 feet of you. A deafening blast erupts from that point. Each creature within a 10-foot radius from that point must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature made of inorganic material such as stone, crystal, or metal has disadvantage on this saving throw. On a failure, a target takes {@dice 4d8} thunder damage and is {@condition Deafened} for 10 minutes. On a success, a creature takes half as much damage and is not {@condition Deafened}. A creature {@condition Deafened} in this way may remake the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on themselves on a success. A nonmagical object that isn't being worn or carried also takes the damage if it's in the blast. You can increase this ability’s damage by {@dice 1d8} per additional psi point spent on it.

{@b Storm (5 psi; conc., 10 min.)} As a bonus action, choose a point above you that you can see within 120 feet of you in which a 10 foot tall, 60-foot radius cylinder could fit. A storm cloud then appears with those dimensions, centered on that point. The area beneath the cloud is no longer considered to be in direct sunlight. Additionally, on each of your turns until the ability ends, you can use psi points to affect creatures and objects under the cylinder, manifesting one of the following effects as an action:

{@b Lightning Strike (1—7 psi)} A bolt of lightning strikes at a point you can see under the cloud. Each creature within a 5 foot radius of that point must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@dice 1d12} lightning damage per psi point spent or half as much on a success. If the creature is wearing armor made of metal, the creature makes this save at disadvantage.
{@b Rain (1 psi)} The cloud rains, extinguishing exposed flames in the area beneath the cloud.

{@b Tempest (6 psi; conc., 1 min.)} As an action, choose a point you can see within 90 feet of you. A powerful storm cloud sweeps through the area in a 20-foot radius sphere centered on that point. The area becomes {@quickref difficult terrain||3}, and creatures inside the area are {@condition Deafened} and cannot see more than 5 feet in any direction. Creatures outside of the area cannot see more than 5 feet into the area, and have disadvantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks made to listen while within 30 feet of the area. Additionally, on each of your turns until the ability ends, you can use psi points to affect creatures within the sphere, manifesting one of the following effects as an action:

{@b Lightning Surge (1—7 psi)} Each creature in the sphere must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@dice 1d6} lightning damage per psi point spent or half as much on a success. If the creature is wearing armor made of metal, the creature makes this save at disadvantage.

{@b Roaring Winds (1—7 psi)} Each creature in the sphere must make a Strength saving throw, taking {@dice 1d4} bludgeoning damage per psi point spent or half as much on a success. Additionally, for each creature that fails, the creature is pulled 5 feet towards the center of the sphere per psi point spent and knocked {@condition Prone}.
{@b Thunderous Crack (1—7 psi)} Each creature in the sphere must make a Constitution saving throw, taking {@dice 1d10} thunder damage per psi point spent or half as much on a success.

{@b Roaring Thunder (7 psi)} As an action, choose a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Thunder energy erupts in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature made of inorganic material such as stone, crystal, or metal has disadvantage on this saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@dice 8d6} thunder damage, and it is {@condition Stunned} until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage and is not {@condition Stunned}. A nonmagical object that isn't being worn or carried also takes the damage if it's in the blast.

optionalfeature.name: Aura Sight
entries: {@i Awakened Discipline}
You refocus your sight to see the energy that surrounds all creatures. You perceive auras, energy signatures that can reveal key elements of a creature’s nature.

items: {@b Psychic Focus.} While focused on this discipline, you add {@dice 1d4} to the result of any Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks made by you.
{@b Read Moods (1 psi)} As a bonus action, you learn a one-word summary of the emotional state of up to three creatures you can see, such as happy, confused, afraid, or violent.

{@b Assess Foe (3 psi)} As a bonus action, you attempt to analyze the aura of one creature you see. The target makes a Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check contested by your Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check. On a success, you learn its creature type, whether or not it is bloodied, and all its immunities, resistances, and vulnerabilities.

{@b Aura Sight (5 psi; conc., 1 hr.)} As an action, you gain the ability to see auras even of {@condition Invisible|phb} or hidden creatures. Until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends, you can see all creatures, including hidden and invisible ones, regardless of lighting conditions. Creatures blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt are immune to this perception.

{@b Decipher Aura (5 psi; conc., 1 hr.)} As an action, you study one creature’s aura. Until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends, while you can see the target, you learn if it’s under the effect of any magical or psionic effects, its creature type, whether or not it is bloodied, and its basic emotional state. While this effect lasts, you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks you make against it.

optionalfeature.name: Bestial Form
entries: {@i Immortal Discipline}
You transform your body, gaining traits of different beasts.

items: {@b Psychic Focus.} While focused on this discipline, you add 1d4 to the result of any Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) checks made by you.

{@b Primal Attack (1—7 psi)} You manifest long claws for an instant and attempt to maul creatures around you, making melee weapon attacks against creatures within your reach, the total number of which is equal to the number of psi points spent. On a hit, each attack deals {@dice 2d6} slashing damage. You cannot do any other actions or movement between attacks.

{@b Bestial Transformation} As an action, you alter your physical form to gain different characteristics. When you use this ability, you can choose one or more of the following effects. Each effect has its own psi point cost. Add them together to determine the total cost. This transformation lasts for 1 hour, until you die, or until you end it as a bonus action.
{@b Amphibious (1 psi)} You gain gills; you can breathe air and water.

{@b Claws (1 psi)} You temporarily manifest or sharpen your claws or talons to be used as effective weapons, allowing you to use them to make a special unarmed strike with which you are proficient, dealing slashing damage equal to {@dice 1d4} + your Strength modifier on a hit, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike. You may also attack with the claws in your offhand if it is free to do so as a bonus action, though you do not add your Strength modifier to the damage roll if you hit with them.
{@b Climbing (2 psi)} You grow tiny hooked claws that give you gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed.
{@b Flight (4 psi)} Wings sprout from your back. You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed.
{@b Keen Senses (2 psi)} Your eyes and ears become more sensitive. You gain advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks.

{@b Perfect Senses (3 psi)} You gain a keen sense of smell and an instinct to detect prey. You can see {@condition Invisible|phb} creatures and objects within 10 feet of you, even if you are {@condition Blinded|phb}.
{@b Swimming (2 psi)} You gain fins and webbing between your fingers and toes; you gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.
{@b Tough Hide (1 psi)} Your skin becomes as tough as leather; your base AC becomes 12 + your Dexterity modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Brute Force
entries: {@i Immortal Discipline}
You augment your natural strength with psionic energy, granting you the ability to achieve incredible feats of might.

items: {@b Psychic Focus.} While focused on this discipline, you add {@dice 1d4} to the result of any Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks made by you.

{@b Brute Strike (1—7 psi)} As a bonus action, you augment your physical strength as you hit a target with a melee weapon attack. You gain a bonus to the damage equal to {@dice 1d8} per psi point spent, and the bonus damage is the same type as the attack. If the attack has more than one damage type, you choose which one to use for the bonus damage.

{@b Knock Back (1—7 psi)} When you hit a target with a melee attack, you can use a bonus action to deliver a shockwave that potentially knocks the target back. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked 10 feet away from you per psi point spent. The target moves in a straight line. If it hits an object, this movement immediately ends and the target takes {@dice 1d6} bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet that it was prevented from moving.

{@b Mighty Leap (1—7 psi)} As part of your movement, you jump in any direction up to 20 feet per psi point spent. A jump done with this feature may be split up between several turns if you do not have the movement to accomplish it in a single turn, but the movement from the jump must be consecutive between turns. Once the movement from the jump is over, you fall as normal.
{@b Feat of Strength (2 psi)} As a reaction, you gain a bonus to a Strength check equal to your Intelligence modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Celerity
entries: {@i Soulknife Discipline}
You channel psionic power into your body, honing your reflexes and agility to an incredible degree. The world seems to slow down while you continue to move as normal.

items: {@b Psychic Focus.} While focused on this discipline, you add {@dice 1d4} to the result of any Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) checks made by you.

{@b Blur of Motion (1—7 psi)} As an action, you cause yourself to be so quick that you become a formless blur during any of your movement during the current turn. You increase your walking speed by 10 feet per psi point spent until the end of the current turn. If you have a climbing or swimming speed, this increase applies to that speed as well. Additionally, creatures that attack you while you’re moving do so at disadvantage, and you only provoke opportunity attacks from creatures that saw you either at the beginning of your turn or during any breaks between your movement this turn.
{@b Agile Defense (2 psi)} As a bonus action, you take the {@action Dodge|phb} action.
{@b Continious Agility (2 psi)} As an action, your movement speed increases by 10 feet for 1 hour.

{@b Surge of Speed (2 psi)} As a bonus action, until the end of your current turn, you gain the benefits of the {@action Dash|phb} and {@action Disengage|phb} actions, and you double your jump distance for the turn.

{@b Slippery Movement (6 psi)} As an action, you imbue your body with a wily cunning for 1 hour. You are unaffected by {@quickref difficult terrain||3} and are immune to effects that would reduce your speed, including the {@condition Paralyzed|phb} and {@condition Restrained|phb} conditions. Additionally, you can spend 5 feet of movement to automatically escape from nonmagical restraints, such as manacles or a creature that has you grappled. Finally, being underwater imposes no penalties on your movement or attacks.

optionalfeature.name: Corrosive Metabolism
entries: {@i Immortal Discipline}
Your control over your body allows you to deliver acid or poison attacks.

items: {@b Psychic Focus.} While focused on this discipline, any acid or poison damage you take is reduced by 2.

{@b Corrosive Touch (1—7 psi)} As an action, you deliver a touch of acid to one creature within your reach. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@dice 1d10} acid damage per psi point spent on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

{@b Venom Strike (1—7 psi)} When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can use a bonus action to make the attack laced with venom, forcing the target to make a Constitution saving throw On a failure, the target takes {@dice 1d8} poison damage per psi point spent and is also {@condition Poisoned|phb} for one minute. On a success, the target takes half as much poison damage and is not {@condition Poisoned|phb}. A creature {@condition Poisoned|phb} by this ability can remake the Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

{@b Acid Blood (3 psi)} As a reaction when you are hit by a melee attack by a creature within 5 feet of you, you cause acid to burst forth and spray from your wound. The creature that struck you takes {@dice 1d8} acid damage and if the weapon that struck you was made of metal, it corrodes. After dealing damage, the weapon takes a permanent and cumulative −1 penalty to damage rolls. If its penalty drops to −5, the weapon is destroyed.

{@b Toxic Spray (3 psi)} As an action, you spray a toxic shot that targets one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. Make a ranged spell attack against a creature within range. On a hit, the creature takes {@dice 3d8} poison damage and is {@condition Poisoned|phb} for 1 minute. At the end of the target’s turns while it is {@condition Poisoned|phb} in this way, they must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature takes {@dice 3d4} poison damage. On a success, the creature is no longer {@condition Poisoned|phb}.

{@b Breath of the Black Dragon (5—7 psi)} You exhale a wave of acid in a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@dice 10d6} acid damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. You can increase the damage by {@dice 1d6} per additional psi point spent on it.

{@b Breath of the Green Dragon (7 psi)} You exhale a cloud of poison in a 90-foot cone. Each creature in the line must make a Constitution saving throw, taking {@dice 10d6} poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

optionalfeature.name: Crown of Despair
entries: {@i Avatar Discipline}
You have learned to harvest seeds of despair in a creature’s psyche, wracking it with self-doubt and inaction.

items: {@b Psychic Focus.} While focused on this discipline, you can use a bonus action to attempt to weaken an opponent’s mental defenses. Target one creature within 30 feet of you that you can see. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the creature subtracts {@dice 1d4} from the next Wisdom saving throw that it makes until the end of your next turn. On a success, the creature is immune to the effects of this focus for 24 hours.

{@b Drown in Ennui (1—7 psi)} As an action, one creature you can see within 60 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@dice 1d6} psychic damage per psi point spent, it can’t take reactions, and its speed is halved until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

{@b Call to Inaction (2 psi; conc., 10 min.)} If you spend 1 minute conversing with a creature, you can attempt to seed it with overwhelming ennui. At the end of the minute, you can use an action to force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw. The save automatically succeeds if the target is immune to being {@condition Charmed|phb}. On a failed save, it sits and is {@condition Incapacitated|phb} until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends. This effect immediately ends if the target or any ally it can see is attacked or takes damage. On a successful save, the creature is unaffected and has no inkling of your attempt to bend its will, but it may think less of you depending on its personality.

{@b Visions of Despair (3—7 psi)} As an action, you force one creature you can see within 60 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@dice 3d6} psychic damage, and its speed is reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. You can increase the damage by {@dice 1d6} per additional psi point spent on it.

{@b Dolorous Mind (6 psi; conc., 1 min.)} As an action, you choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or it is {@condition Incapacitated|phb} and has a speed of 0 until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends. It can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

{@b Drain Hope (7 psi; conc., 1 min.)} As an action, you choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or it takes {@dice 1d10} psychic damage, drops @condition{Prone}, and is {@condition Incapacitated|phb} with a speed of 0 until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends. It spends its turns wallowing in self-pity and loathing, hating every part of itself. It can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, taking {@dice 1d10} psychic damage on a failure or ending the effect on itself on a success.

optionalfeature.name: Crown of Disgust
entries: {@i Avatar Discipline}
You cause a creature to be flooded with emotions of disgust.

items: {@b Psychic Focus.} While focused on this discipline, you can use a bonus action to attempt to weaken an opponent’s mental defenses. Target one creature within 30 feet of you that you can see. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the creature subtracts {@dice 1d4} from the next Charisma saving throw that it makes until the end of your next turn. On a success, the creature is immune to the effects of this focus for 24 hours.

{@b Incite Nausea (1—7 psi)} As an action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@dice 1d6} poison damage per psi point spent and is {@condition Poisoned|phb} for 1 minute. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and is not {@condition Poisoned|phb}. A creature {@condition Poisoned|phb} by this ability can remake the Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

{@b Repulsive Presence (1—7 psi)} As an action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@dice 1d8} psychic damage per psi point spent and can’t move closer to you until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

{@b Wall of Repulsion (3 psi; conc., 10 min.)} As an action, you create an invisible, insubstantial wall of energy within 60 feet of you that is up to 30 feet long, 10 feet high, and 1 foot thick. The wall lasts until your {@status concentration||concentration} ends. Any creature attempting to willingly move through it must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a creature can’t move through the wall until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, the creature can pass through it. A creature must make this save whenever it willingly attempts to pass through the wall.

{@b Visions of Disgust (5 psi; conc., 1 min.)} As an action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The target must make an Intelligence saving throw.
